title: S04 GBP Update: Hamilton County list prices are down from a year ago
hook: Hamilton County's median list price is about $30,000 lower than it was a year ago.
body:
In October, the median list price across Hamilton County was $445,000. Last fall, sellers were asking noticeably more.

What that means if you are buying in Fishers, Carmel, Noblesville or Westfield: you may find homes in neighborhoods that felt just out of reach a year ago, and you have more listings to compare while you decide.

What it means if you are selling: buyers are watching prices closely. A home that is priced right from day one, and looks cared for, still stands out.

Keep in mind this is a list price, the asking price, not what homes sold for. Your street and your home's condition can tell a different story than the county median.

Source: Realtor.com via FRED, Oct 2026.

title: S05 Email: Buyer newsletter, more homes to choose from this winter
subject: Indy buyers have 21% more homes to pick from this winter
preview: 7,171 homes were for sale across the metro in October. Here is how to use that in a calm winter search.
hook: If last spring's house hunt felt like a sprint, this winter may feel more like a walk.
body:
Hi {{first_name}},

If last spring's house hunt felt like a sprint, this winter may feel more like a walk.

## More homes on the shelf

In October, 7,171 homes were listed for sale across the Indianapolis-Carmel-Anderson metro. That is 21.3% more than a year earlier, according to Realtor.com data via FRED. Hamilton County followed the same pattern, with active listings up 19.3%.

## What that means for you

More homes for sale usually means fewer bidding wars and more time to think. You can compare a few homes side by side, ask for a repair after inspection, or talk about closing costs without feeling the clock run out. Every home and every seller is different, so we look at each one on its own.

One Fishers buyer put it this way: "They never tried to upsell or pressure us to move faster than we were comfortable." That is the pace we aim for with everyone.

## A word on rates

Rates still matter. But the right time to buy depends on your monthly comfort level, your cash for closing, and how long you plan to stay, not on guessing where rates go next. A lender pre-approval shows you real numbers for your situation.

## Your next step

Hit reply and tell us your top must-haves and the towns you are watching, whether that is Fishers, Carmel, Noblesville or Westfield. We will set up a winter search that sends you only the homes that fit.

Warmly,

The Evelo Team

hook: A closing in Noblesville can end with clean water for a family in need.
body:

It is not a holiday campaign. It happens on every closing, all year long. It is our way of living out the words we started with in 1998: Making a Difference. Changing Lives. Leaving a Legacy.

title: S20 GBP Update: Promote the winter-vs-spring selling blog post
hook: Tempted to wait for spring before you list your Hamilton County home? Your own timeline matters more than the calendar.
body:
One thing has clearly changed this year: buyers have more to choose from. Hamilton County had 1,111 active listings in October, up 19.3% from a year earlier.

When buyers have options, price and presentation do more of the work in any season. A well-prepared winter listing in Fishers or Carmel can stand out to the buyers who are still shopping, while a spring listing may share the stage with more homes.

Our new post, "Should You Sell Your Hamilton County Home in Winter or Wait for Spring?", walks through what a winter listing gains, what it gives up, and how to decide based on your own plans. It is a calm, plain-English read, written for homeowners, not agents.

Source: Realtor.com via FRED, Oct 2026.

title: S30 GBP Update: Year-end metro snapshot, list price per square foot
hook: Here is the year-end number that surprised us: across the Indy metro, list prices per square foot went up, not down.
body:
The median list price per square foot in the Indianapolis-Carmel-Anderson metro was $164 in October, up 5.1% from a year earlier.

That can sound odd next to headlines about lower list prices. The difference is the mix of homes. When more smaller or lower-priced homes come on the market, the overall median list price can dip even while each square foot is listed for more.

The takeaway: a metro headline will not tell you much about your own home. Size, condition and location matter more. If you are buying, compare homes by price per square foot, not just the sticker price. If you are selling, start with the homes most like yours in your part of Hamilton County.

Source: Realtor.com via FRED, Oct 2026.
